title: 采莲曲（荷叶罗裙一色裁）
author: 王昌龄
intro: Girls picking lotus blend so well into the pond — green skirts like leaves, faces like flowers — that you can only tell they are there when you hear them sing.
analysis: 这首诗写江南水乡的姑娘们划船采莲。第一句说姑娘的绿色罗裙和荷叶好像是用同一块布裁出来的，颜色一样；第二句说荷花（芙蓉）向着她们的脸开放，花和脸一样红润好看。人和荷花融成了一体，分不清哪是花、哪是人。第三句写她们的小船划进密密的荷塘，一下子就看不见了；第四句却说：听到歌声，才知道有人来了。诗人没有正面描写姑娘长什么样，而是用“人花难分”来写她们的美，这是一种很巧的侧面描写；最后用声音点出人物，画面里一下子有了动感和欢乐。全诗明快活泼，像一幅会唱歌的画。
analysisEn: This poem shows girls in the water country south of the Yangtze rowing out to pick lotus. Line one says their green silk skirts and the lotus leaves look as if they were cut from the same cloth; line two says the lotus flowers open toward their faces, flowers and faces equally rosy. Girls and flowers merge, and you can’t tell which is which. Then their little boats slip into the thick of the pond and disappear completely — and only when singing drifts out do you realise someone is there. The poet never describes the girls directly. Instead he shows their beauty by making them impossible to tell apart from the lotus, a clever indirect approach; and by bringing them back through sound at the end, he fills the still picture with movement and fun. Lotus picking was a real summer job in the south, but in the poem it feels like a game of hide-and-seek. Bright and playful, it is like a painting that suddenly starts to sing.
background: Wang Changling (c. 698–757) was a leading High Tang poet. “Lotus-Picking Song” is an old yuefu song title going back to the Southern Dynasties; Wang wrote two poems under it, of which this is the second and better known.
pronunciation: 无特殊读音。注意：一色 yī sè；看不见 kàn bù jiàn（按本调标注）；始觉 jué。
version: 采用通行本（《全唐诗》）。原作两首，这是第二首。

lines.py: hé yè luó qún yī sè cái
lines.lit: Lotus leaves and silk skirts are cut from one colour;
lines.en: Lotus leaves and silk skirts, cut from the same green,

lines.py: fú róng xiàng liǎn liǎng biān kāi
lines.lit: lotus flowers open toward faces on both sides.
lines.en: lotus blooms open beside faces just as pink.

lines.py: luàn rù chí zhōng kàn bù jiàn
lines.lit: Mixing into the pond, they cannot be seen;
lines.en: They melt into the pond and are lost from sight —

lines.py: wén gē shǐ jué yǒu rén lái
lines.lit: hearing songs, only then do you sense someone is coming.
lines.en: only a song tells you someone is there.

words.note: 这里指荷花，不是木芙蓉。

words.en: to mix into; to blend in among

words.note: 古义“听见”；现代汉语“闻”多指用鼻子闻，“新闻”还保留“听说”的意思。
古义“才”；现代汉语“开始”“始终”。

imagery.name: 莲
imagery.zh: 荷叶、荷花和采莲姑娘融为一体，荷花衬出姑娘的美丽。
imagery.en: Lotus leaves and flowers blend with the girls, and the blossoms set off their beauty.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 满是荷叶的池塘藏起了小船和姑娘，只留下歌声在水面上飘。
imagery.en: The pond full of leaves hides the boats and girls; only their song floats over the water.
